# Set-Up the Discretization/Initialization Function for the Model
def discretize_initialize(m, nfe):
    """Discretize and initialize model.

    Inputs:
        m: Model to discretize.
        nfe: Number of finite elements

    Returns:
        m: Discretized model.

    """

    # Check dimensional consistency BEFORE discretizing.
    #
    # This is the last moment at which the check is meaningful. The collocation
    # equations added on the next line multiply state variables by numerical
    # reciprocal-delta-t coefficients that carry no units, because a
    # ContinuousSet cannot hold any -- Pyomo issue #1790, still open:
    #   https://github.com/Pyomo/pyomo/issues/1790
    # Asserting after `apply_to` raises InconsistentUnitsError on a model that is
    # perfectly correct. See ./units_and_pyomo_dae.md
    assert_units_consistent(m)

    # Transform the Model using the 'dae.collocation' strategy.
    discretizer = pyo.TransformationFactory("dae.collocation")
    discretizer.apply_to(m, nfe=nfe, wrt=m.t)  # default ncp = 3

    # Specify Initial Conditions
    m.h[0].fix(0)
    m.v[0].fix(0)

    return m


# Set-Up Solve Function
def solve_model(m, tee=True):
    """Solves model with ipopt.

    Inputs:
        m: Model to solve.
        tee: Whether to print full output

    Returns:
        m: Solved model.

    """

    # Specify Solver
    solver = pyo.SolverFactory("ipopt")
    # Solve the Model
    results = solver.solve(m, tee=tee)
    assert pyo.check_optimal_termination(results), (
        f"Solve failed: status={results.solver.status}, "
        f"termination={results.solver.termination_condition}"
    )

    return m

def visualize_model(m):
    """Plotting model function with publication quality for main plots
    used in notebook.

    v = [pyo.value(m.v[i]) for i in m.t]
    D = [pyo.value(m.D[i]) for i in m.t]
    L = [pyo.value(m.L[i]) / 1000 for i in m.t]  # plotting in kN

    fig, axs = plt.subplots(3, 1, dpi=200, figsize=(8, 12.8))

    colors = okabeito_list
    # Plot Height vs Time
    axs[0].plot(t, h, label="height_model", linewidth=3, color=colors[0])
    axs[0].set_ylabel("Height (m)", fontweight="bold", fontsize=16)

    # Plot Velocity vs Time
    axs[1].plot(t, v, linewidth=3, color=colors[0])
    axs[1].set_ylabel("Velocity (m/s)", fontweight="bold", fontsize=16)

    # Lift (m/s^2) vs time
    axs[2].plot(t, L, linewidth=3, color=colors[0])
    axs[2].set_xlabel("Time (s)", fontweight="bold", fontsize=16)

    axs[1].tick_params(direction="in", labelsize=15)
    axs[2].tick_params(direction="in", labelsize=15)

# Set up our model as a function
def create_balloon_model_v0():
    """Model function. All other models are modified versions.
    Inputs: None
    Returns:
        m: Base model to be discretized, initialized, solved, and plotted."""

    # Create a Pyomo Model
    m = pyo.ConcreteModel("Hot Air Balloon")

    # Define Time Domain. NOTE: a ContinuousSet cannot carry units (Pyomo issue
    # #1790), so the seconds live in this comment. Bounds are in SECONDS.
    m.t = dae.ContinuousSet(bounds=(0, 100))

    # Define Fixed Control Input
    m.L = pyo.Var(m.t, initialize=10000, units=units.N)  # Newtons

    # Define State Variables as Functions of Time
    m.h = pyo.Var(m.t, bounds=(0, None), units=units.m)  # height
    m.v = pyo.Var(m.t, units=units.m / units.s)  # vertical velocity
    m.D = pyo.Var(m.t, units=units.N)  # drag force

    # DerivativeVar defaults to DIMENSIONLESS and does NOT inherit units from the
    # state variable. m.t is time in seconds, so state it: dh/dt is m/s and
    # dv/dt is m/s^2.
    m.dhdt = dae.DerivativeVar(m.h, wrt=m.t, units=units.m / units.s)
    m.dvdt = dae.DerivativeVar(m.v, wrt=m.t, units=units.m / units.s**2)

    # Define Differential Constraints
    @m.Constraint(m.t)
    def dh_con(m, t):
        return m.dhdt[t] == m.v[t]

    @m.Constraint(m.t)
    def dv_con(m, t):
        return m.dvdt[t] * m_balloon == m.L[t] - m_balloon * g - m.D[t]

    # Define Algebraic Constraints
    @m.Constraint(m.t)
    def drag_con(m, t):
        return m.D[t] == b * m.v[t] ** 2

    # Define L
    @m.Constraint(m.t)
    def l_con(m, t):
        return m.L[t] == 10000 * units.N

    return m

# Set-Up our Model as Function
def create_balloon_model_v1():
    """Modified from v0. Fixed drag."""

    # A velocity-scale epsilon that removes the |v| singularity at v = 0.
    # It is compared against v, so it must carry v's units.
    eps = 1e-6 * units.m / units.s

    # Create a Pyomo Model
    m = pyo.ConcreteModel("Hot Air Balloon")

    # Define Time Domain. NOTE: a ContinuousSet cannot carry units (Pyomo issue
    # #1790), so the seconds live in this comment. Bounds are in SECONDS.
    m.t = dae.ContinuousSet(bounds=(0, 100))

    # Define State Variables as Functions of Time
    m.h = pyo.Var(m.t, bounds=(0, None), units=units.m)  # height
    m.v = pyo.Var(m.t, units=units.m / units.s)  # vertical velocity
    m.D = pyo.Var(m.t, units=units.N)  # drag force

    # Define Fixed Control Input
    m.L = pyo.Var(m.t, initialize=500, units=units.N)

    # DerivativeVar defaults to DIMENSIONLESS and does NOT inherit units from the
    # state variable. m.t is time in seconds, so state it: dh/dt is m/s and
    # dv/dt is m/s^2.
    m.dhdt = dae.DerivativeVar(m.h, wrt=m.t, units=units.m / units.s)
    m.dvdt = dae.DerivativeVar(m.v, wrt=m.t, units=units.m / units.s**2)

    # Reformulate m.D to Add Stability
    @m.Constraint(m.t)
    def drag_con(m, t):
        return m.D[t] == b * (m.v[t] ** 2 + eps**2) ** (1 / 2) * m.v[t]

    # Define Differential Constraints
    @m.Constraint(m.t)
    def dh_con(m, t):
        return m.dhdt[t] == m.v[t]

    @m.Constraint(m.t)
    def dv_con(m, t):
        return m.dvdt[t] * m_balloon == m.L[t] - m_balloon * g - m.D[t]

    # Define L

    @m.Constraint(m.t)
    def l_con(m, t):
        return m.L[t] == 10000 * units.N

    return m

def create_balloon_model_v2(height_ref):
    """Fixed drag, added objective for difference of final height from height ref, squared.

    Input:
        height_ref: Reference desired final height (m).

        Returns:
        m: Initial model v2.
    """

    # Set a Target Height
    desired_height = height_ref * units.m
    endtime = 200  # seconds

    # A velocity-scale epsilon that removes the |v| singularity at v = 0.
    # It is compared against v, so it must carry v's units.
    eps = 1e-6 * units.m / units.s

    # Create a Pyomo Model
    m = pyo.ConcreteModel("Hot Air Balloon")

    # Define Time Domain. NOTE: a ContinuousSet cannot carry units (Pyomo issue
    # #1790), so the seconds live in this comment. Bounds are in SECONDS.
    m.t = dae.ContinuousSet(bounds=(0, endtime))

    # Define State Variables as Function of Time
    m.h = pyo.Var(m.t, bounds=(0, None), units=units.m)  # height
    # NOTE: Var bounds are NOT units-checked by assert_units_consistent.
    # These are m/s, and only this comment says so.
    m.v = pyo.Var(m.t, bounds=(-2, 5), units=units.m / units.s)
    m.D = pyo.Var(m.t, units=units.N)  # drag force

    # Define Control Variable (Lift) as a Function of Time
    m.L = pyo.Var(m.t, bounds=(L_lb, L_ub), units=units.N)

    # DerivativeVar defaults to DIMENSIONLESS and does NOT inherit units from the
    # state variable. m.t is time in seconds, so state it: dh/dt is m/s and
    # dv/dt is m/s^2.
    m.dhdt = dae.DerivativeVar(m.h, wrt=m.t, units=units.m / units.s)
    m.dvdt = dae.DerivativeVar(m.v, wrt=m.t, units=units.m / units.s**2)

    # Define Derivative Constraints
    # Height derivative constraint (dh/dt = v)
    @m.Constraint(m.t)
    def dh_con(m, t):
        return m.dhdt[t] == m.v[t]

    # Velocity derivative, acceleration constraint (m * dv/dt = L - mg - D)
    @m.Constraint(m.t)
    def dv_con(m, t):
        return m.dvdt[t] * m_balloon == m.L[t] - m_balloon * g - m.D[t]

    # Drag force calculation (D = b * v^2)
    @m.Constraint(m.t)
    def drag_con(m, t):
        return m.D[t] == b * (m.v[t] ** 2 + eps**2) ** (1 / 2) * m.v[t]

    # Set Initial conditions
    m.h[0].fix(0)
    m.v[0].fix(0)
    m.L[0].fix(10000)  # newtons -- .fix() values are not units-checked either

    # Define the objective: Minimize the difference between final height and the desired height
    @m.Objective(sense=pyo.minimize)
    def objective(m):
        return (
            m.h[endtime] - desired_height
        ) ** 2  # Minimize squared difference at final time

    return m

    # A velocity-scale epsilon that removes the |v| singularity at v = 0.

    # Define Time Domain. NOTE: a ContinuousSet cannot carry units (Pyomo issue
    # #1790), so the seconds live in this comment. Bounds are in SECONDS.
    m.t = dae.ContinuousSet(bounds=(0, tf))

    # Define State Variables as Function of Time
    m.h = pyo.Var(m.t, bounds=(0, None), units=units.m)  # height
    m.v = pyo.Var(m.t, units=units.m / units.s)  # vertical velocity
    m.D = pyo.Var(m.t, units=units.N)  # drag force

    # Define Control Variable (Lift) as a Function of Time
    m.L = pyo.Var(m.t, bounds=(L_lb, L_ub), units=units.N)

    # DerivativeVar defaults to DIMENSIONLESS and does NOT inherit units from the
    # state variable. m.t is time in seconds, so state it: dh/dt is m/s and
    # dv/dt is m/s^2.
    m.dhdt = dae.DerivativeVar(m.h, wrt=m.t, units=units.m / units.s)
    m.dvdt = dae.DerivativeVar(m.v, wrt=m.t, units=units.m / units.s**2)

    # Define Derivative Constraints
    # Height derivative constraint (dh/dt = v)
    @m.Constraint(m.t)
    def dh_con(m, t):
        return m.dhdt[t] == m.v[t]

    # Velocity derivative, acceleration constraint (m * dv/dt = L - mg - D)
    @m.Constraint(m.t)
    def dv_con(m, t):
        return m.dvdt[t] * m_balloon == m.L[t] - m_balloon * g - m.D[t]

    @m.Constraint(m.t)

def create_balloon_model_v4():

    # A velocity-scale epsilon that removes the |v| singularity at v = 0.
    # It is compared against v, so it must carry v's units.
    eps = 1e-6 * units.m / units.s

    # Create a Pyomo Model
    m = pyo.ConcreteModel("Hot Air Balloon")

    # Define Time Domain. NOTE: a ContinuousSet cannot carry units (Pyomo issue
    # #1790), so the seconds live in this comment. Bounds are in SECONDS.
    m.t = dae.ContinuousSet(bounds=(0, tf))

    # Define State Variables as Function of Time
    m.h = pyo.Var(m.t, bounds=(0, None), units=units.m)  # height
    m.v = pyo.Var(m.t, units=units.m / units.s)  # vertical velocity
    m.D = pyo.Var(m.t, units=units.N)  # drag force

    # Define Control Variable (Lift) as a Function of Time
    m.L = pyo.Var(m.t, bounds=(L_lb, L_ub), units=units.N)

    # DerivativeVar defaults to DIMENSIONLESS and does NOT inherit units from the
    # state variable. m.t is time in seconds, so state it: dh/dt is m/s and
    # dv/dt is m/s^2.
    m.dhdt = dae.DerivativeVar(m.h, wrt=m.t, units=units.m / units.s)
    m.dvdt = dae.DerivativeVar(m.v, wrt=m.t, units=units.m / units.s**2)

    # Define Derivative Constraints
    # Height derivative constraint (dh/dt = v)
    @m.Constraint(m.t)
    def dh_con(m, t):
        return m.dhdt[t] == m.v[t]

    # Velocity derivative, acceleration constraint (m * dv/dt = L - mg - D)
    @m.Constraint(m.t)
    def dv_con(m, t):
        return m.dvdt[t] * m_balloon == m.L[t] - m_balloon * g - m.D[t]

    # Define Algebraic Constraints
    # Drag force calculation (D = b * v^2)
    @m.Constraint(m.t)
    def drag_con(m, t):
        return m.D[t] == b * (m.v[t] ** 2 + eps**2) ** (1 / 2) * m.v[t]

    # Define the objective: Minimize the difference between final height and the desired height
    @m.Integral(m.t)
    def ise(m, t):
        # r(t) interpolates the reference path and returns a bare float in metres;
        # `t` is the raw ContinuousSet index, so attach the units here.
        return (m.h[t] - r(t) * units.m) ** 2

    # Define the objective function
    @m.Objective(sense=pyo.minimize)
    def objective(m):
        return m.ise

    # Set Initial conditions
    m.L[0].fix(10000)  # newtons (.fix() values are not units-checked)

    return m

Instead of defining a PID Controller, we implemented the equations of motion for a hot-air balloon in Pyomo and used an objective function to control the decision variable, lift.

The Charm Lab at Stanford only investigated the ascent of a balloon as it traveled to a set height. They did not account for the balloon moving downward; thus, their formulation could not be extended to path planning. We extended their formulation by modifying the Drag equation and defining a flight path for a balloon to reach a set of heights during the balloon’s ascent and descent.
